findings.detail: The capture `ReturnedReasoning` (head ~248-275) reads a caller-supplied `reasoning` string or `reasoning_details` text from each message. At head 360-361 that text is written into `reasoning_content` for assistant turns. `validateHistory(request.messages)` at head 351 runs on SDK-decoded messages, and the SDK message drops these fields. The diff therefore shows no delimiter screening of the injected text. The documented contract says the policy rejects ambiguous native delimiters. A consumer (ADV-002) could embed GLM native tokens such as `</think>`, role markers or `<tool_call>` in a `reasoning` field. That could forge turn or tool-call structure in the rendered prompt and skew provider recount or prompt-contract identity relative to the coordinator's `prompt_work`. The impact is mostly confined to the caller's own request, and the GLM tokenizer may already treat this text safely; that behavior is outside the evidence. Fix: apply the same native-delimiter or ambiguity validation used for `reasoning_content` and content to the captured returned-reasoning strings before they are templated. Then add a regression test.
findings.title: Captured returned reasoning enters the GLM template without the native-delimiter check applied to history
